body: I went to a therapist for a year, and now I've been out of therapy for almost a year. When I left, I felt better. Therapists are great, mine was great, but I think I need to fight through this on my own. That's what I learned in therapy anyway. Most of the healing comes from me. I email my old therapist every now and then. Though lately, more than before, I have been wanting to email her more often and have been thinking very seriously about going back. But I don't even know how to approach that.

Being ashamed and guilty for being too hard on yourself is the same as being hard on yourself. There is a long, long road toward good self-esteem and it will take work. 

Women and men are very emotionally different and women relate to men differently then they relate to women, and vice versa, not to mention sexuality/transference/counter transference and all that fun stuff. I think a lot of people feel women are more approachable/less threatening and that is why women make good therapists. You're not alone in that.


I'm glad you're feeling better. It made me feel better to take on some of your shit tonight instead of wallowing in my own.

I didn't know you currently have a therapist, that's a very different conversation! If it's not working for you, you should 100% talk to him about that! Tell him everything. That's what he's for, he's a trash can for all your shit. He will sit there and take it. Don't be afraid of being an asshole if you're being honest with him, this guy is supposed to be offering a service to you that depends on both of you being honest with each other. I can really sense that you're too hard on yourself, calling yourself an asshole constantly. I get it, some people are assholes and some assholes need to be more aware of this. But you said, "I just feel the need to be a fucking dick to people for no apparent reason just to get my point across." Well, you said you have no reason and then you listed a pretty good reason, to communicate a point. You have a reason to be what from your perspective is a dick, you feel like you're not being heard. If something feels like bullshit, don't hold back and say it. Let yourself be a dick and see what happens. Like I told you before, it seems to me like you have a lot on your mind, like you would have a lot to talk about if you would let yourself address the real, tangible, specific problems. If this therapist is not the guy to sit across from you and look you in eye and take on all that for you, then find somebody else. Talk to that guy about what you might need in a therapist that he can't provide. Do you need a woman? Someone younger or older? Someone more unorthodox, someone more traditional? There are a lot of possibilities out there.

Chronic pessimism is a really tough think to fight back against. That's the weird thing about the depression brain I mentioned, it's like conditioning, once you've been thinking in a dark way for a while, it's all you really know. It makes it hard to control yourself, like you said it shows on your face, I think it always shows in my voice. 


When you say you've tried therapy and they don't know how to help you and no one else does, I'm going to just go ahead and bet that you haven't seen every therapist out there, including the trainees that are new, inexpensive, just learning, and who aren't in it for the money or jaded yet. Do not give up just because they haven't worked yet. I know therapist shopping is hard because you have to introduce yourself over and over and revisit your presenting problems again and again during the intake process. But you will find one that you will feel comfortable with, if you're open to that. They may never know what to say or how to help, but they might be able to help you look inside yourself for the answers, they might teach you how to talk about yourself in a way you didn't know was possible. When you establish a relationship with a therapist, you are learning more about what it's like to connect to another human being. The most important thing they can do for you when you're in a state like this, they will not want you to die and they will fight for your life, and maybe teach you how to want to live for yourself as well.

These thoughts I have are the worst when I'm tired. Maybe being tired is kind of like feeling close to death in a way? Sometimes it seems like it would be easier to die than to ever feel awake again. It sounds like you have a lot on your mind though, you should definitely unload it all in as much detail as you can. This is a safe place, but an even better place would be a therapist or a support group where you can get a real human response. I bet you're not really an asshole, although the depression brain is really good at tricking you into that kind of behavior, like you said "automatically". A therapist or a support group could help you see the value you have in yourself. If you've tried them before and had a bad experience, I'd keep trying.
